"The Self is already attained, it is already perfect, it is already filled with bliss. There is nothing to be attained anew. You have only to recognize what is already there."
"I came into the garden of this world, and marveled at the roses and thorns. I looked within myself and saw that I was the gardener, the garden, and the act of looking."
"The yogi who perceives the entire universe as a play of his own consciousness finds no distinction between the sacred and the mundane — every act becomes an act of worship, every breath a prayer."
"Citi (universal consciousness) itself, descending from its state as Citi, becomes the mind by contracting in accordance with the objects of knowledge."
"My Guru gave me but one precept: 'Turn your gaze from the external world and fix it on the Inner Self.' Taking that to heart, I, Lalla, naked set forth to dance."
"I searched for myself and found only God; I searched for God and found only myself."
"The nature of one's own Self, which is pure consciousness, is not something to be sought elsewhere. It shines by its own light, and its recognition is liberation itself."

"Spanda is that slight movement or throb in the absolute stillness of pure consciousness — not a movement in space or time, but the very life of awareness itself, the divine creative pulsation from which the entire universe arises and into which it dissolves."

"The lake of my mind, hit by hailstones of experience, went dark and turbulent. But when I turned within and found the spring of stillness, the hailstones melted into clarity, and I saw that the water had always been pure."

"Just as a mirror, though reflecting many images, remains pure and unchanged in itself, so the Lord, though manifesting this entire universe, remains ever pure, ever still, ever the same supreme consciousness."

"Shiva is not to be worshipped in temples alone. He resides in your own awareness — in the awareness that is aware of itself. When that awareness turns back upon itself and recognizes its own nature, that very recognition is liberation."

"What is this world? What is it that is to be abandoned or accepted? Where is the void, where is the plenum? The whole expansion of this universe is none other than the expansion of Shiva's own nature."
"I, Lalla, entered the jasmine garden through the gate of the breath. There I saw Shiva and Shakti locked in embrace — and realized there was no gate, no garden, no entering. Only this."

"Consciousness is the nature of the Self. It is self-luminous, self-revealing, and self-established. It does not require any other light to illumine it, for it is the very source of all illumination — and in that recognition, the seeker and the sought dissolve into one undivided light."

"Wherever the mind goes, whether toward the external world or toward the inner world, everywhere it finds only Shiva. For the enlightened one, there is no going out and no coming in — there is only the One, shining in all directions."

"The universe is a living mirror of the divine — not a veil to be pierced, but a radiance to be recognized. Every form, every sound, every sensation is Shiva's own delight in knowing Himself through the play of appearance."

"The flame of the lamp dispels darkness and reveals the objects in a room. But consciousness is self-luminous — it reveals itself and all else by its own light alone. To know this is to know everything."

"The divine Spanda is not different from Shiva, the supreme consciousness. It is the very heart of reality, eternally throbbing with the pulse of recognition — and when the awakened one perceives this vibration in the arising and dissolving of all things, he stands rooted in that stillness which is the source of all movement."
"I, Lalla, wearied myself searching and striving. I looked and looked for Him — and then, all at once, found that He had been with me all along, closer than my own breath, nearer than my own self."
"The experient of limited knowledge, though in reality identical with universal consciousness, becomes the object of his own experience by contracting his infinite power of consciousness."
"The light of consciousness that illumines the world is not in the world — it is the very eye that sees. To search for it with the mind is like the sun going out with a lamp to find the daylight."

"The divine light of Shiva is not somewhere far away. It is the very pulse of your own awareness — and the moment you stop running toward the horizon and simply rest in what you are, that pulse is felt, and in that feeling, everything is recognized."

"Lalla was absorbed in the search for herself. She abandoned modesty, gave up shame, and kept only the company of the wise. Then the light of the Self, which had always been shining, was recognized — and in that recognition, Lalla disappeared, and only the light remained."

"The Lord is the knower, and the known, and the act of knowing. He is the seer, the seen, and the act of seeing. He is the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and the act of enjoyment. In this recognition, all duality collapses into the singular light of awareness."

"The body is my temple, the breath is my prayer. I do not go to the river to bathe — I bathe in the river of the Self. Lalla has no caste, no creed, no scripture — only this naked flame of knowing, which neither wind nor water can extinguish."

"He who realizes the truth of his own Self as Shiva — the absolute, the infinite, the self-luminous — is not born again, nor does he die. For him, what is there to attain? He has become the very ground of all attainment."

"The individual self and the universal Self are not two. When the veil of difference is lifted, what remains is the one undivided consciousness — and that lifting is not an achievement but a recognition, like the sky recognizing that it was never truly divided by the clouds that passed through it."
"The whole universe is perceived in one's own consciousness just as the city is seen in a mirror. The Shiva-state is that illuminated consciousness which is one's own self."
"Whatever form one contemplates as suffused with the bliss of the Self, one should stabilize that very state. Then, O gazelle-eyed one, the supreme bliss of yoga will arise of itself."

"The Śiva-state is not something to be achieved through effort or constructed through practice. It is your own nature, already and always present — and the recognition of this is itself the supreme initiation."
"The divine light is not something separate from you that you must seek and find. You are that light — and the recognition of this fact, even for a moment, is worth more than a lifetime of seeking."
"The Self is its own means of attainment. There is no other means."

"The heart of the devotee is the real Shiva-linga. The limbs are the temple. The mind is the priest. The self-luminous awareness within is the flame of the lamp. With this knowledge, what need is there to search for Shiva elsewhere?"
"Chiti (consciousness-force) is the cause of the siddhi (accomplishment) of the universe. The universe is reflected in it as in a mirror."
"The Self, which is pure awareness, has contracted itself into the form of the individual out of its own free will — and that same free will, turned inward, becomes the means of its own recognition."

"My Guru gave me but one precept: 'Turn your gaze from the without to the within.' I obeyed, and now I abide in the nakedness of pure awareness — beyond birth, beyond death, beyond the reach of sorrow."

"The Self is not to be sought by the eye, not by speech, not by the other senses, not by austerity, not by ritual. When the intellect is cleansed, one sees that indivisible Self by the grace of meditation — and that seeing is the end of all seeking."

"Chiti (universal consciousness) descending from the plane of Shiva, becomes the universe by contracting its infinite powers of consciousness in conformity with the object it cognizes. The same Chiti, by its own nature, ascending again to the plane of Shiva, brings about the recognition of the already-accomplished Self."

"Spanda is that slight movement of consciousness — like the throb of joy in one who is absorbed — which is the very heart of reality. It is not a movement from place to place, but the eternal pulsation of awareness knowing itself, and in that knowing, becoming everything."

"Akula (Shiva, the supreme) is like a burning flame. Kula (the universe) is like the fuel which feeds that flame. In reality, however, the flame and the fuel are not two different things — the universe is nothing but the very life of Shiva, burning as the world."
"I searched for myself and found only God. I searched for God and found only myself."

"The yogi who is always united with Shiva, whether waking, dreaming, or in deep sleep — for him the three states are dissolved into a fourth, and that fourth pervades and illumines all the rest. He does not leave the world to find God; he finds that the world itself is the shining of God."
"Lalla drank the water of the Ganges of the Self — and her thirst was quenched forever. She had been carrying water from the river to the sea, not knowing that the sea was already within her."
"The knowable dissolves, the knower dissolves — and what remains is the pure act of knowing, which was never born and never dies. That knowing is Shiva, and that Shiva is you."

"The knowledge of the Self is not something acquired from without. It wells up from within, like a spring that has always been flowing beneath the ground — and when the ground breaks open, one does not say 'I have found water.' One says only: 'It was always here.'"
